review_notes:
I read the whole file (lines 1–275). It has no new definitions, no @[simp] or @[simp↓] attributes, no simp sets, and no custom simp lemmas. It contains eight theorems about conditional expectation. Their conclusions are a.e. equalities, an a.e. equality to a constant, or an lintegral inequality. They have non-trivial hypotheses: σ-finiteness of a trim, integrability, L¹ convergence, and 0-or-1 measure conditions. Those are poor simp-lemma candidates, and the rubric says not to recommend simp annotations just because an identity looks simple.

Inside the proofs, simp is only called on small local goals: `simp [hω]`, `simpa using this`, and the final `simpa [eLpNorm_eq_lintegral_rpow_enorm_toReal, ...]` in `lintegral_enorm_condExp_rpow_le`. I saw no sign of a rewrite loop, competing rules, or unwanted expansion in any of them. I did not run Lean, so I cannot say whether any of these simp calls is fragile. I did not look through Mathlib for existing simp lemmas to compare against, because there was no candidate to compare.
